Jealousy can arise when a valued relationship or object is in danger of being damaged or lost, especially when a rival seems involved.

## Words describing jealousy

Cautious, clinging, clutching, defensive, fear of losing someone or something, mistrustful, possessive, rivalrous, self-protective, suspicious, wary, and watchful.

## Prompting events and interpretations

Events include a threatened relationship, a potential competitor, or attention given elsewhere. Interpretations may predict betrayal, rejection, inferiority, abandonment, or not being cared for.

## Body changes, expressions, and action urges

Breathlessness, fast heartbeat, a lump in the throat, muscle tension, suspicion, rejection, helplessness, or injured pride may appear. Urges and actions can include controlling, clinging, interrogating, accusing, spying, gathering evidence, or threatening a rival.

## Aftereffects

Attention can narrow toward relationship threats, with mistrust, hypervigilance, isolation, or withdrawal.

## When jealousy fits the facts

Jealousy fits when a very important relationship or object is genuinely in danger of being damaged or lost.

## Acting on the urge, Opposite Action, and Checking the Facts

When the threat is real, use effective communication, boundaries, or problem solving. When it is not, let go of controlling behaviour, stop spying or probing, take in all available information, and act from supported trust.
